title: 望天门山
author: 李白
intro: The Yangtze River smashes through two mountains, and a single sail comes gliding out of the sunrise. A young Li Bai paints a whole landscape — in motion — in four lines.
analysis: 天门山是长江边上隔江相对的两座山，远远看去像一道天上的大门。第一句说，长江像一把巨斧，把天门山从中间劈开，江水冲了过去；第二句说，碧绿的江水向东奔流，到了这里却被山挡得打着旋儿转回来。一“开”一“回”，写出了江的力量和山的险要。第三句最妙：明明是船在走，诗人却说两岸青山“相对出”，好像山自己迎面走出来——这是坐在船上看到的真实感觉。最后，一片孤帆从太阳那边驶来，画面一下子开阔明亮。全诗二十八个字，有山有水，有动有静，颜色鲜明，像一幅会动的山水画。
analysisEn: Heaven’s Gate is a pair of mountains facing each other across the Yangtze, like the two posts of a giant gate. In the first line the river seems to split the mountain in two and burst through. In the second, the clear green water racing east is forced by the cliffs to swirl and turn back. One verb shows the river’s power (开, “to open”), the other the mountains’ strength (回, “to turn back”). The third line is the cleverest. It is really the boat that moves, yet the poet says the green mountains on both banks “come out” to meet each other — exactly what you feel sitting on a moving boat. Finally a single sail glides in from where the sun is rising, and the whole scene opens up into light and space. In twenty-eight characters we get mountains and water, motion and stillness, green, blue and gold — like a landscape painting that moves. It is a favourite in Chinese primary schools.
background: Li Bai (701–762) is traditionally said to have written this around 725, aged about 25, when he left Sichuan and sailed down the Yangtze for the first time. Heaven’s Gate Mountains stand on the river near today’s Ma’anshan in Anhui.
version: 采用统编小学语文教材文本，与维基文库《全唐诗》本一致。“至此回”一作“直此回”（“回”文库作繁体“迴”），网站不用。

lines.py: tiān mén zhōng duàn chǔ jiāng kāi
lines.lit: Heaven’s Gate breaks in the middle; the Chu River opens it;
lines.en: Heaven’s Gate is split in two where the great river forces through;

lines.py: bì shuǐ dōng liú zhì cǐ huí
lines.lit: the green water flows east and, reaching here, turns back.
lines.en: the green water rushing east swirls back against the cliffs.

lines.py: liǎng àn qīng shān xiāng duì chū
lines.lit: Green mountains on both banks come out facing each other;
lines.en: On either bank, green mountains step out face to face,

lines.py: gū fān yī piàn rì biān lái
lines.lit: a single lone sail comes from beside the sun.
lines.en: and one lone sail comes gliding from the sun.

words.en: Heaven’s Gate (two mountains facing each other across the Yangtze)
words.note: 地名，在今安徽马鞍山、芜湖一带。
这里指山从中间断开；今天“中断”多指事情中途停止。

words.en: the Chu River (the Yangtze where it flows through old Chu)
words.note: 指流经古代楚国一带的长江。
现代汉语“碧绿”“碧蓝”里还用。
书面语，现代汉语说“到这里”。
指江水被山挡住打旋、转向。
山“走出来”，其实是船在前进。
诗词常用词，“帆”今天也说“船帆”。

words.en: beside the sun; where the sun is
words.note: 指远处天边太阳的方向。

imagery.name: 山
imagery.zh: 天门山被江水劈开，又迎面“走”来，写出山的雄伟和旅途的新鲜感。
imagery.en: The mountains, split by the river and seeming to walk towards the boat, show both their grandeur and the thrill of travel.

imagery.name: 长江
imagery.zh: 长江冲开大山、回旋奔流，充满力量。
imagery.en: The Yangtze bursts through the mountains and swirls back — pure power.

imagery.name: 帆
imagery.zh: 日边驶来的孤帆让画面开阔明亮，也带着诗人自己出行的豪情。
imagery.en: The lone sail from the sunrise opens the scene into light and space, carrying the young poet’s own excitement at setting out.
